sentences.text: "3. Definition of domestic violence.--For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence

or danger to life, limb, or health or impair the health or development of the aggrieved person
and includes assault, criminal intimidation and criminal force;

59. POINT No.3:

In the instant case, the petitioner/aggrieved has sought the following reliefs:-
a) Pass an order prohibiting and preventing the respondent from committing any act of domestic violence at the present residence of the petitioner and create nuisance in the vicinity.
b) Direct the officer in charge of the jurisdiction police station and give protection to the petitioner from the respondent.

c) Pass an order directing the respondent to pay Rs.25 crores as permanent alimony or a permanent Crl. Misc.No.74/2017 maintenance of Rs.2,50,000/- p.m. by way of compensation towards mental agony, torture, physical harassment, medical expenses.
60.In the case on hand
the petitioner is claiming the relief of protection order and monetary reliefs from the respondent, admittedly from 2011 to the date of filing of this petition the parties are residing separately.

As discussed earlier the petitioner in the instant case has failed to prove the act of domestic violence, A conjoined reading of Section 12 and section 2(a) makes it abundantly clear that relief under the DV act can be granted only to an aggrieved person defined under the DV act and an aggrieved person has been defined as a woman who is or has been in a domestic relationship with the respondent who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent.
Therefore, proving of allegation of domestic violence is a sine qua non for pursuing a petition under the Dv act.

61.Now the question is whether the wife who failed to prove commission of domestic violence against her husband will be entitled to a relief under Section 12 of the DV Act in view of my discussion in previous point she is not entitle for any protection order since she fail to prove the commission of domestic violence.

Therefore, unless it is shown that the aggrieved person and/or her child has suffered such a loss, no order of monetary relief can be passed under the D.V.
Act.
63.

In the case on hand both the parties have filed assets and liability affidavit and both side contended that they have not disclosed true details , upon perusal both side not disclosed complete information before the court, the contention of the petitioner counsel that the respondent has not disclosed the investments in shares, debentures and mutual funds and non disclosure of property at tumkur Industrial area holds good, inn similar manner the contention of the respondent that she admitts about trust and bank acccount and she has not disclosed the same and the fixd deposits which she had is not disclosed is also true further the court noticed that in her HDFC bank account the petitioner is frequently drawing money by using sweep in credit.
A sweep in credit, or sweep account, is a bank arrangement that automatically moves excess funds in an account to an investment or debt repayment account.

This can help Crl. Misc.No.74/2017 customers earn interest on their money and reduce their interest costs on debts, to have that facility she must be premium customer of the bank and had either investments in bank or fixed deposits.

HDFC banks sweep-in facility ensures that whenever funds in Savings Account are running low for a purchase or transaction, the bank will transfer the deficit amount from your Fixed Deposit to savings account without affecting interest rate in your Fixed Deposit.
Which means there is a fixed deposit in that bank and petitioner is utilizing the same but she did not mention the same in assets column.
64. Upon closer scrutiny of material available on record and in the light of aforementioned position of law, I am of the opinion that she failed to prove she is aggrieved woman as per the definition.
Hence the reliefs are declined.
After having arrived at a conclusion that the very basis on which an alleged domestic violence had set up had crumbled down, there was no scope for granting any consequential reliefs.
In view of the above reasons, I answer Point No.3 in Negative.

The petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is hereby dismissed.
